requirements.heading: Checking Authorization
requirements.text: Without explicit approval of the publishing ADMD, checking other identities against SPF version 1 records is NOT RECOMMENDED because there are cases that are known to give incorrect results.

requirements.heading: Checking Authorization
requirements.text: To make the test, the mail receiver MUST evaluate the check_host() function with the arguments described in Section 4.1.

requirements.heading: The "HELO" Identity
requirements.text: It is RECOMMENDED that SPF verifiers not only check the "MAIL FROM" identity but also separately check the "HELO" identity by applying the check_host() function (Section 4) to the "HELO" identity as the <sender>.

requirements.heading: The "HELO" Identity
requirements.text: Checking "HELO" before "MAIL FROM" is the RECOMMENDED sequence if both are checked.

requirements.heading: The "MAIL FROM" Identity
requirements.text: SPF verifiers MUST check the "MAIL FROM" identity if a "HELO" check either has not been performed or has not reached a definitive policy result by applying the check_host() function to the "MAIL FROM" identity as the <sender>.

requirements.heading: Location of Checks
requirements.text: The authorization check SHOULD be performed during the processing of the SMTP transaction that receives the mail.

requirements.heading: DNS Resource Records
requirements.text: SPF records MUST be published as a DNS TXT (type 16) Resource Record (RR) [RFC1035] only.

requirements.heading: Multiple DNS Records
requirements.text: A domain name MUST NOT have multiple records that would cause an authorization check to select more than one record.

requirements.heading: Multiple Strings in a Single DNS Record
requirements.text: If a published record contains multiple character-strings, then the record MUST be treated as if those strings are concatenated together without adding spaces.

requirements.heading: Record Size
requirements.text: The published SPF record for a given domain name SHOULD remain small enough that the results of a query for it will fit within 512 octets.

requirements.heading: Wildcard Records
requirements.text: In particular, the declaration MUST be repeated for any host that has any RR records at all, and for subdomains thereof.

requirements.heading: The check_host() Function
requirements.text: A compliant SPF implementation MUST produce results semantically equivalent to this description.

requirements.heading: The check_host() Function
requirements.text: Receiving ADMDs that perform this check MUST correctly evaluate the check_host() function as described here.

requirements.heading: The check_host() Function
requirements.text: Implementations MAY use a different algorithm than the canonical algorithm defined here, so long as the results are the same in all cases.

requirements.heading: Initial Processing
requirements.text: Internationalized domain names MUST be encoded as A-labels, as described in Section 2.3 of [RFC5890].

requirements.heading: DNS Lookup Limits
requirements.text: SPF implementations MUST limit the total number of those terms to 10 during SPF evaluation, to avoid unreasonable load on the DNS.

requirements.heading: DNS Lookup Limits
requirements.text: If this limit is exceeded, the implementation MUST return "permerror".

requirements.heading: DNS Lookup Limits
requirements.text: In addition to that limit, the evaluation of each "MX" record MUST NOT result in

requirements.heading: DNS Lookup Limits
requirements.text: If this limit is exceeded, the "mx" mechanism MUST produce a "permerror" result.

requirements.heading: DNS Lookup Limits
requirements.text: In addition to that limit, the evaluation of each "PTR" record MUST NOT result in querying more than 10 address records -- either "A" or "AAAA" resource records.

requirements.heading: DNS Lookup Limits
requirements.text: If this limit is exceeded, all records other than the first 10 MUST be ignored.

requirements.heading: DNS Lookup Limits
requirements.text: MTAs or other processors SHOULD impose a limit on the maximum amount of elapsed time to evaluate check_host().

requirements.heading: DNS Lookup Limits
requirements.text: Such a limit SHOULD allow at least 20 seconds.

requirements.heading: DNS Lookup Limits
requirements.text: If such a limit is exceeded, the result of authorization SHOULD be "temperror".

requirements.heading: DNS Lookup Limits
requirements.text: SPF implementations SHOULD limit "void lookups" to two.

requirements.heading: DNS Lookup Limits
requirements.text: An implementation MAY choose to make such a limit configurable.

requirements.heading: DNS Lookup Limits
requirements.text: In this case, a default of two is RECOMMENDED.

requirements.heading: "all"
requirements.text: Mechanisms listed after "all" MUST be ignored.

requirements.heading: "all"
requirements.text: Any "redirect" modifier (Section 6.1) MUST be ignored when there is an "all" mechanism in the record, regardless of the relative ordering of the terms.

requirements.heading: "mx"
requirements.text: To prevent denial-of-service (DoS) attacks, the processing limits defined in Section 4.6.4 MUST be followed.

requirements.heading: "mx"
requirements.text: Note regarding implicit MXes: If the <target-name> has no MX record, check_host() MUST NOT apply the implicit MX rules of [RFC5321] by querying for an A or AAAA record for the same name.

requirements.heading: "ptr" (do not use)
requirements.text: This mechanism SHOULD NOT be published.

requirements.heading: "ptr" (do not use)
requirements.text: To prevent DoS attacks, the PTR processing limits defined in Section 4.6.4 MUST be applied.

requirements.heading: "ptr" (do not use)
requirements.text: If used, proper PTR records have to be in place for the domain's hosts and the "ptr" mechanism SHOULD be one of the last mechanisms checked.

requirements.heading: "ptr" (do not use)
requirements.text: It is, however, still in use as part of the SPF protocol, so compliant check_host() implementations MUST support it.

requirements.heading: Modifier Definitions
requirements.text: The modifiers defined in this document ("redirect" and "exp") SHOULD appear at the end of the record, after all mechanisms, though syntactically they can appear anywhere in the record.

requirements.heading: Modifier Definitions
requirements.text: These two modifiers MUST NOT appear in a record more than once each.

requirements.heading: Modifier Definitions
requirements.text: Unrecognized modifiers MUST be ignored no matter where, or how often, they appear in a record.

requirements.heading: Modifier Definitions
requirements.text: For clarity, any "redirect" modifier SHOULD appear as the very last term in a record.

requirements.heading: Modifier Definitions
requirements.text: Any "redirect" modifier MUST be ignored if there is an "all" mechanism anywhere in the record.

requirements.heading: Modifier Definitions
requirements.text: If no "exp" modifier is present, then either a default explanation string or an empty explanation string MUST be returned to the calling application.

requirements.heading: Modifier Definitions
requirements.text: Implementations MAY limit the length of the resulting explanation string to allow for other protocol constraints and/or reasonable processing limits.

requirements.heading: Modifier Definitions
requirements.text: Since the explanation string is intended for an SMTP response and Section 2.4 of [RFC5321] says that responses are in [US-ASCII], the explanation string MUST be limited to [US-ASCII].

requirements.heading: Modifier Definitions
requirements.text: Software SHOULD make it clear that the explanation string comes from a third party.

requirements.heading: Modifier Definitions
requirements.text: Note: During recursion into an "include" mechanism, an "exp" modifier from the <target-name> MUST NOT be used.

requirements.heading: Modifier Definitions
requirements.text: In contrast, when executing a "redirect" modifier, an "exp" modifier from the original domain MUST NOT be used.

requirements.heading: Macro Processing Details
requirements.text: Some older implementations of SPF prohibit trailing dots in domain names, so trailing dots SHOULD NOT be published, although they MUST be accepted by implementations conforming to this document.

requirements.heading: Macro Processing Details
requirements.text: If a DIGIT is specified, the value MUST be nonzero.

requirements.heading: Macro Processing Details
requirements.text: Implementations MUST support at least a value of 127, as that is the maximum number of labels in a domain name (less the zero-length label at the end).

requirements.heading: Macro Processing Details
requirements.text: If the <domain> is present in the list of validated domains, it SHOULD be used.

requirements.heading: Macro Processing Details
requirements.text: Otherwise, if a subdomain of the <domain> is present, it SHOULD be used.

requirements.heading: Macro Processing Details
requirements.text: This macro SHOULD NOT be published (see Section 5.5 for the discussion).

requirements.heading: Macro Processing Details
requirements.text: This SHOULD be a fully qualified domain name, but if one does not exist (as when the checking is done by a Mail User Agent (MUA)) or if policy restrictions dictate otherwise, the word "unknown" SHOULD be substituted.

requirements.heading: Macro Processing Details
requirements.text: URL escaping MUST be performed for characters not in the "unreserved" set, which is defined in [RFC3986].

requirements.heading: Neutral
requirements.text: A "neutral" result MUST be treated exactly like the "none" result; the distinction exists only for informational purposes.

requirements.heading: Fail
requirements.text: If the checking software chooses to reject the mail during the SMTP transaction, then it SHOULD use an SMTP reply code of 550 (see [RFC5321]) and, if supported, the 5.7.1 enhanced status code (see [RFC3463], Section 3.8), in addition to an appropriate reply text.

requirements.heading: Fail
requirements.text: If the checking software chooses not to reject the mail during the SMTP transaction, then it SHOULD add a Received-SPF or Authentication-Results header field (see Section 9) to communicate this result to downstream message processors.

requirements.heading: Softfail
requirements.text: Receiving software SHOULD NOT reject the message based solely on this result, but MAY subject the message to closer scrutiny than normal.

requirements.heading: Temperror
requirements.text: If the message is rejected during the SMTP transaction for this reason, the software SHOULD use an SMTP reply code of 451 and, if supported, the 4.4.3 enhanced status code (see Section 3.5 of [RFC3463]).

requirements.heading: Permerror
requirements.text: If the message is rejected during the SMTP transaction for this reason, the software SHOULD use an SMTP reply code of 550 and, if supported, the 5.5.2 enhanced status code (see [RFC3463], Section 3.6).

requirements.heading: Recording the Result
requirements.text: To provide downstream agents, such as MUAs, with the information they might need in terms of evaluating or representing the apparent safety of the message content, it is RECOMMENDED that SMTP receivers record the result of SPF processing in the message header.

requirements.heading: The Received-SPF Header Field
requirements.text: The Received-SPF header field is a trace field (see [RFC5322], Section 3.6.7) and SHOULD be prepended to the existing header, above the Received: field that is generated by the SMTP receiver.

requirements.heading: The Received-SPF Header Field
requirements.text: It MUST appear above all other Received-SPF fields in the message.

requirements.heading: The Received-SPF Header Field
requirements.text: The header field SHOULD include a "(...)" style comment after the result, conveying supporting information for the result, such as <ip>, <sender>, and <domain>.

requirements.heading: The Received-SPF Header Field
requirements.text: SPF verifiers SHOULD give enough information so that the SPF results can be verified -- that is, at least "client-ip", "helo", and, if the "MAIL FROM" identity was checked, "envelope-from".

requirements.heading: The Received-SPF Header Field
requirements.text: Other keys MAY be defined by SPF verifiers.

requirements.heading: The Received-SPF Header Field
requirements.text: SPF verifiers MUST make sure that the Received-SPF header field does not contain invalid characters, is not excessively long (see [RFC5322], Section 2.1.1), and does not contain malicious data that has been provided by the sender.
